title: The Flat Box
subtitle: A furniture company asked its customers to do something strange: carry the furniture home in pieces and build it themselves. Why did millions of people say yes?

vocab.def: To put the parts of something together to make it.
vocab.ex: I assembled the table in one hour.

vocab.def: A book or magazine with pictures and prices of things you can buy.
vocab.ex: She looked at the catalogue and chose a chair.

vocab.def: A room or shop where a company shows its products.
vocab.ex: We saw the sofa in the showroom.

vocab.def: To be the right size and shape for a space.
vocab.ex: The box does not fit in my car.

vocab.def: A person who plans how something will look and work.
vocab.ex: The designer drew a new chair.

vocab.def: A very big building where a company keeps its goods.
vocab.ex: The boxes are in the warehouse.

vocab.def: To take goods to a customer's home or office.
vocab.ex: They will deliver the bed on Monday.

vocab.def: To keep money, or to spend less money.
vocab.ex: You can save money if you carry it home yourself.

vocab.def: Words and pictures that tell you how to do something.
vocab.ex: Read the instructions before you start.

vocab.def: Broken or not perfect because something hit it.

vocab_discuss: Have you ever put together a table, a bed or a shelf yourself? How was it?
Would you carry furniture home yourself to pay less? Why or why not?
What is the most difficult thing you have ever made or built?

story.heading: Part 1 — A very young businessman
paras: In 1943, a seventeen-year-old boy from Sweden started a small company. His name was Ingvar Kamprad. He called it IKEA. The name came from his own initials and the first letters of his family's farm and village.

At first, Ingvar did not sell furniture. He sold small things, like pens and picture frames, and people ordered them by post. In 1948, he began to sell furniture. He used a catalogue with pictures and prices, and customers sent their orders.

But there was a problem. Customers wanted to touch and see the furniture before they bought it. So in the 1950s, IKEA opened a showroom in the small town of Älmhult, and in 1958 it opened its first big store there.
tf: Ingvar Kamprad started IKEA when he was an old man.
At first, IKEA sold small things by post.
The first big IKEA store opened in 1958.
discuss: Why do customers like to see furniture before they buy it?
Would you start a company at seventeen? What would you sell?

story.heading: Part 2 — The problem with big furniture
paras: Furniture is big and heavy. A finished table needs a lot of space in a warehouse, and a lot of space in a truck. Delivery is expensive, and the furniture often arrives damaged. All this makes the price higher.

In 1956, the story says, a young IKEA designer called Gillis Lundgren had a simple idea. He wanted to put a table into his car, but the table did not fit. So he took the legs off. Suddenly, the table was flat, and it fitted easily.
Kamprad liked the idea very much. IKEA began to sell furniture in flat boxes. The customer took the box home and assembled it with a small tool and a page of instructions.
tf: Finished furniture is easy and cheap to move.
The designer took the legs off a table to fit it in his car.
In a flat box, the customer must put the furniture together.
discuss: What is good about furniture in a flat box? What is bad?
Do you think the table story is true? Why does the story work so well for the company?

story.heading: Part 3 — Why it worked
paras: The flat box was a clever bet, because it made things cheaper in many places. A flat box takes less space in the warehouse and in the truck. It breaks less often. And the customer does the last job — carrying it home and building it — so IKEA does not need to deliver it.
All this means IKEA can save money, and it can give the customer a lower price. People did not mind building the furniture, because it was much cheaper.

There was a risk. Some people hated the instructions and the missing screws. But many customers felt proud when the furniture stood in their room. Today IKEA has stores in dozens of countries. One of its simplest products, the Billy bookcase, has sold more than a hundred million.
The lesson is clear: if you ask customers to do some work, give them a good reason, like a much lower price.
tf: A flat box takes more space in a truck.
The customer's work helps IKEA to keep prices low.
Nobody had a problem with the instructions.
discuss: Which jobs do customers do today that workers did before? (Think about shops, banks and airports.)
What is the good reason for the customer in IKEA's idea?

grammar.name: has / have been + -ing
grammar.heading: Something that started in the past and continues now: has been growing, have been waiting
explain: The story of IKEA is a story of things that started a long time ago and are still going on. For this we use the present perfect continuous.
Form: have / has + been + verb-ing → IKEA has been selling furniture since 1948. / Customers have been building their own furniture for many years.
for + a length of time: for sixty years, for a long time, for two hours. since + a starting point: since 1958, since Monday, since I was a child.
Questions: How long have you been working here? / How long has the company been growing?
Be careful: if you say when something finished or happened, use the past simple: IKEA opened its first store in 1958. (not has been opening in 1958)
Remember: for and since are different. for ten years ✓ / since ten years ✗

head: Time word
Meaning
Example
rows: The company has been growing for sixty years.

practice.heading: Put the verb in the present perfect continuous
practice.intro: Write have/has + been + the verb with -ing. Use the correct form of have/has.
items: 1. IKEA ___ (make) flat-pack furniture for more than sixty years.
2. Customers ___ (carry) boxes out of the store since this morning.
3. The designer ___ (work) on the new chair since January.
4. How long have you ___ (wait) for the delivery? (Write two words.)
5. We ___ (build) this bookcase for two hours, and it is still not finished.

fix.heading: Find the mistake
items: The company has been grow fast since 1990.
She has been working here since five years.
IKEA has been opening its first store in 1958.
How long you have been waiting for the table?
The customers has been carrying the boxes all morning.
answers: The company has been growing fast since 1990. (been + -ing)
She has been working here for five years. (for + a length of time)
IKEA opened its first store in 1958. (a finished event with a date = past simple)
How long have you been waiting for the table? (question order)
The customers have been carrying the boxes all morning. (customers = have)

speak.label: 1 · Tell the story
paras: Tell me the IKEA story in order, from 1943 to today. Use for and since at least twice. Six or seven sentences is enough.

speak.label: 2 · The missing screw
paras: Role play. Person A bought a bookcase in a flat box and cannot assemble it. Person B works in the shop.
A: Explain the problem. Say how long you have been trying.
B: Ask questions and offer help.
helper: How long have you been trying?
I have been building it since…

speak.label: 3 · How long?
paras: Ask and answer: How long have you been doing your job, your hobby or your studies? Ask three more How long questions.

speak.label: 4 · The customer's job
paras: Think of a business where the customer does a small job to get a lower price. Explain the idea. What does the customer do? What does the company save?

final: Is it fair to ask customers to do work for a lower price? When is it OK and when is it not?
Why did the flat box work for IKEA? Could it work for other products, like cars or clothes?
Look at your own job. What has your company been doing for years that it could do in a new way?
